080 · /map redesign — design comp for operator review
plans/mockups/080-network-decision-map · real 2026-03 release data · 350 routes · not production UI

A network map New Yorkers would actually read

The operator review of the live /map: hard to tell the lines apart, no obvious place to focus without a route in mind, everything outside Manhattan reads as one green mass, the All day / AM / PM toggle barely changes anything, and the popup stat “Lanes 6%” explains nothing. Every one of those has a measurable cause in the current encoding — none of them is a data problem. This comp diagnoses each, then proposes a redesign on plan 080’s interaction skeleton. Every map below renders the real March 2026 release artifacts (350 routes, borough context, NYC DOT bus-lane centerlines) — nothing is invented.

ComplaintMeasured causeFix in this comp
“Everything is green” The ramp saturates to full green at 7.8 mph — but 223 of 350 routes are at or above it, and 149 are past the ramp’s 9.5 end entirely. Staten Island’s median is 13.1 mph. The scale was built for Manhattan (median 6.5) and throws away the rest of the city. Color only marks slow: under-7 mph ember, 7–8 sienna — everything typical-or-faster rides one baseline ink. Green is gone, and so is the rainbow. Exhibits B & C.
“Toggle does nothing” Median route shifts only 0.6 mph between all-day and PM peak — invisible on a near-flat ramp, with no transition and no summary of what changed. At PM peak the slowest band grows 65 → 110 routes — red visibly spreads — and the legend counts move with it; a caption states the shift; plus a proposed “vs all day” compare mode. Exhibit D.
“Lanes 6%” It’s the share of the route’s shape overlapping a DOT bus-lane street (median 12%) — unlabeled, denominator unstated, and the lane lens paints a green gradient over green routes. Lanes become a real geometry layer (the 3,048 DOT centerlines), the lens is retired, and the popup spells the stat out. Exhibit E.
“Where do I focus?” 350 identical 2.2px lines, zero labels, zero landmarks, no ranking, nothing pinned. A search-first “Find a route” panel (opt-in, closes on pick), route badges on the worst ten, borough & water labels, and a rider-delay lens that surfaces the real story — the B6 loses ≈140,000 rider-hours in March, more than any Manhattan route. Exhibits B & F.
Standing rulings respected No autoplay or hour-scrubber (rejected 2026-07-04, removed in 9789242) — period changes are single discrete transitions. No external tiles/CDN; all cartography is first-party artifacts. Lane-coverage stays a labeled fact, never a composite “treatment gap” score (076 gate). No new pages or tabs — this upgrades /map in place. Copy uses “Data through March 2026”, never month-identity or banned phrases.
Relationship to plan 080 080 already specifies the skeleton this comp assumes: URL state, search, pin-don’t-navigate, ranked DOM list, desktop inspector / mobile sheet, feature-state hover, borough labels, real bus-lane layer, Data notes. This comp supplies the visual system 080 left open — scales, palettes, hierarchy, legend, popup — plus three amendment candidates flagged in the decision table (D7, D15, D17).
A · BEFORE

What ships today, re-rendered from the live artifacts

same 350 routes, current ramp and line weights
One story, told badly. The ramp’s only message is “Manhattan slow, everywhere else fine” — which every New Yorker already knows. 64% of the network shares one green; the slowest borough gets all the contrast.
The legend numbers (3/5/7/9/11+) are the interface. They’re speed-bin endpoints doing the work of a scale, with no sense of what’s typical — nothing tells you 8.7 mph is the citywide median.
No anchors. No borough names, no water names, no route names, no ranking. If you don’t already know the city’s shape, there is nowhere to start reading.
B · REDESIGN

“Atlas” — the redesign on a light surface

interactive: hover, click to pin, switch lens/period, open “Find a route”
D1Attention scale. Only slower-than-typical routes get color — under 7 mph glows ember, 7–8 runs sienna; the 210 typical-or-faster routes ride baseline ink. Color stops decorating and starts pointing.
D3Badges answer “where do I look?” The ten worst routes for the active lens carry MTA-style route pills on the line itself — always on, no checkbox. Everything else stays legible; nothing is dimmed by default (080 rule).
D4Opt-in, search-first. The map opens clean — no persistent sidebar. One “Find a route” pill opens a panel with search, borough chips and the full ranked list; picking a route pins it and the panel gets out of the way. Desktop now mirrors the mobile browse pattern.
D17One-strip legend. Each band is a single segment with its range and live route count inside, sized by the real share. No swatch grid, no tick rows. Switch periods and the counts move — the toggle finally has a visible consequence.
D18The insight note is dismissible — and stays dismissed. The top-right note carries one finding per lens. Its ✕ is remembered as a preference; a small ⓘ brings it back. First-visit guidance, zero permanent chrome.
D13Honest gaps. Routes failing the period coverage gate draw dashed ink, with a legend entry and a count — never silently recolored (6 routes at AM, 3 at PM).
C · REDESIGN

“Signal” — the same bones on a dark surface

recommended default · interactive
D11Dark is the salience model. On near-black water, brightness = urgency: crawling routes glow ember over a smoke-gray baseline network. The eye lands on the problem without anything being dimmed.
The page stays light. Only the map surface goes dark — a framed object in the light app, like a transit diagram on a station wall. No dark-mode fork of the design system; every card, panel and control keeps app tokens.
Why recommend this as default: it kills the green-wash completely, pairs with the black nav, and photographs like a poster — the shareable artifact a portfolio map should be. “Atlas” remains the print/embed variant. Operator call.
D · TIME

Making All day / AM / PM worth touching

static multiples + the proposed compare mode
PM peak vs all day — proposed “compare” mode
Diverging scale: purple = slower at PM peak than the route’s all-day average, teal = faster. Bins at ±0.75 and −1.5 mph. This is the map that makes the toggle’s question — who gets hit at rush hour? — answerable at a glance.
The city’s day, in one striptraversal-weighted mean, all routes
Buses citywide are slowest 2–6 PM (7.2 mph at 14:00–15:00), not the morning rush — school dismissal plus early rush. AM’s worst hour barely dips below midday. This strip sits beside the period control as its explanation.
Why the current toggle feels dead: the median route moves 0.6 mph between periods — on a continuous ramp that’s a few RGB points. With the attention scale, the slowest band swells from 65 to 110 routes at PM peak (67 change band) and the legend counts move; with the compare mode, the change is the color. No autoplay, no scrubber — one discrete, captioned transition per user action, honoring the 2026-07-04 rejection.
E · LANES

Lanes as geometry, not a percentage

the 3,048 real NYC DOT bus-lane centerlines, drawn under the network
Bus-lane layer under the speed lensManhattan & western Queens crop
Dashed green centerlines are the DOT source geometry — labeled as street centerlines, not route coverage. The lane lens (green-on-green gradient) is retired; lanes become a layer you read against speed.
The story the old stat buried Reading lanes against speed is where this product earns its name. Three routes make the case that paint alone isn’t priority — exactly the kind of finding the studies engine exists to test:
M4242nd St crosstown
Bus lanes92%
Speed5.2

The most-laned slow route in the city — 2nd slowest overall despite near-total coverage.

M34+34th St SBS
Bus lanes85%
Speed5.9

Full SBS treatment, still under 6 mph — enforcement and design questions, not coverage.

B1149th/50th St, Brooklyn
Bus lanes3%
Speed6.0

The mirror case: as slow as midtown with almost no priority treatment at all.

Popup rewrite: “Lanes 6%” becomes “Bus lanes along 6% of this route” with the method one tap away (share of route shape overlapping DOT bus-lane streets). No composite score — the 2×2 “slow + unlaned” framing stays a 076-gated spike.
F · RIDERS

The rider-delay lens — where the hours actually go

rider-hours of delay, March 2026 · baseline under 8k, colored 8–15k / 15–40k / 40k+
Rider-hours of delayconstant width
Purple deepens with total rider-hours lost vs schedule across observed segments. The pattern inverts the speed map: the pain is in Brooklyn and Queens locals, not midtown.
Same lens, width by daily ridersproposed option D15
Line width scales with daily ridership (√ scale, 1.3–6.5px). Thick + dark = many people, badly served — the B6, B41, Q25, Q58 corridors become unmissable arteries.
The finding this lens leads with: the B6 (Bensonhurst–East New York) loses ≈140,000 rider-hours in March 2026 — the most in the city, half again the runner-up — while averaging 7.9 mph, a speed the old ramp painted green. Q25, Q58, B41 follow. The rail flips to “Most rider time lost” and the badges follow the lens. This is the map for the “where should the next bus lane go?” conversation — served measures only, no composite.
G · POPUP

The route popup, before and after

click any route in exhibits B/C for the live version
B41
Brooklyn / Kings Plaza - Downtown Brooklyn
7.2 mph
average all-day speed
Riders10k
Lanes17%

Today: three abbreviated stats with no units, no context, no explanation. “Lanes 17%” (flagged) is the operator’s “Lanes 6%” complaint — 17% of what? — and “Delay 101k hr” is just as opaque: 101,000 of what, over when?
D9After: the hero value gets a percentile sentence (“slower than 78% of routes”) — the context line that makes any number mean something. A 24-hour strip shows when it struggles (its slowest stretch marked). Stats get spelled-out labels and windows. Provenance lives behind “Sources”, per the study-card rule — never on the card face.
H · MOBILE

Mobile: browse first, sheet on pin

080’s requirements, styled — static mock
D16“Browse all 350 routes” is always reachable before any pin or search — it opens the same ranked list as the desktop rail, full-height, keyboard- and screen-reader-real (080’s DOM-list rule).
Pin opens a bottom sheet, not a navigation: the same mini-inspector content with title, description, clear action, and “Route detail” as the only navigation. Background tap or Escape clears.
Controls collapse to the Find-a-route pill plus lens and period with 40px targets; the legend docks to the sheet’s collapsed header so the scale never disappears on small screens.
D1–D17

Decision table

status against plan 080 as written
#DecisionStatus vs 080
D1Attention scale for speed: color only marks slower-than-typical — under 7 mph (severe) and 7–8 (slow); everything ≥8 rides one baseline ink. Fixed documented thresholds, invariant across periods/filters. Faster-than-typical differentiation is intentionally dropped; the delay lens carries “where it matters.”fits 080 (fixed documented domain; thresholds are the design)
D2Width hierarchy: base 2.2px, SBS 3.2px, hover/pin 5.5px + casing; salience via color and badges, never via dimming the rest.fits 080
D3Route badges (MTA-style pills) on the worst ten for the active lens, collision-nudged; always on — no toggle.style-only addition
D4080’s ranked DOM list lives behind a “Find a route” pill: an opt-in overlay panel with search, borough chips, rank + pill + corridor + value bar rows (all 350 scrollable), hover/focus sync; picking pins and closes the panel. No persistent desktop sidebar — same browse pattern as mobile.080 amendment candidate (persistent inspector → opt-in panel)
D5Context line “Data through March 2026 · Local, Limited & SBS · 350 of 350 routes · Data notes”.in 080 (amended phrasing)
D6Period switch feedback: single 240ms crossfade (skipped under reduced motion), legend histogram re-proportions, caption states median + class-change count.fits 080 (no autoplay)
D7“Compare: vs all day” mode for AM/PM — diverging Δ scale (±0.75, −1.5 bins). A new documented sub-scale.080 amendment candidate
D8Retire the lane-coverage lens; ship the DOT bus-lane centerline layer (readiness-gated, thin dash over routes, labeled as source geometry). Its switch lives in the Find-a-route panel footer — no floating checkbox chrome.in 080
D9Popup: percentile context sentence, 24h speed strip with slowest-stretch marker, spelled-out stats with windows, Sources popover, Route detail / Studies actions.style-only (structure in 080)
D10Cartography: borough small-caps labels, water labels, coastline hairline, scale bar; no streets, no external tiles.in 080
D11Two surfaces, one system: “Signal” dark map surface (recommended default) and “Atlas” light; page chrome stays light app tokens either way.style-only; default = operator call
D12Paint order by urgency: fastest classes first, slowest last, badges on top — the slow lines sit visually above the fast mass.style-only
D13No-data = dashed ink with legend entry + count; never recolored or hidden.in 080
D14Rider-delay lens, same grammar: baseline under 8k rider-hours; colored steps at 8–15k / 15–40k / 40k+ (March window), purple ramp; ranked list flips to “Most rider time lost”.in 080 (delay-exposure lens; breaks are the design)
D15Optional “width by daily riders” on the delay lens (√ scale 1.3–6.5px), legend-documented.080 amendment candidate
D16Mobile: persistent “Browse all N routes”, pin→bottom sheet with legend docked to its header.in 080
D17One-strip legend: self-labeled bands (range + live route count inside each segment), widths from the real share, dashed no-data chip. No swatch grid, tick rows, or footer. Applies to every lens.080 amendment candidate (legend spec differs from 080’s)
D18Insight note (top-right, one finding per lens) is dismissible; dismissal is remembered as a preference and a small ⓘ restores it.style-only
D19Controls diet: persistent chrome is only the Find-a-route pill, lens, and period segments. No checkboxes on the map surface.style-only
OPEN

Operator questions

1 · Default surface Signal (dark) or Atlas (light) as the shipped default? Comp recommends Signal; both are one config apart.
2 · Compare mode (D7) Approve the “vs all day” diverging mode as an 080 amendment, or hold AM/PM to absolute classes only?
3 · Width-by-riders (D15) Ship with the delay lens, or keep constant width until the lens itself has settled?
4 · Default lens Speed stays the landing lens per 080. Worth reconsidering rider-delay as the landing lens later — it’s the product’s thesis — but that’s a separate call, not assumed here.
